title: Enchiridion Text Metadata
description: Schema for metadata.json files in each text directory

year_written.description: Year originally written/published. Use string for approximate dates (e.g., '~300 BCE', '1905')

year_translated.description: Year of the English translation used, if applicable

language.description: Language of the text file in the repo

original_language.description: Language the work was originally written in

format.description: File format of the text in the repo

layout.description: Optional rendering hint for markdown texts. 'verse' preserves single-newline line breaks for poetry, blank verse, and dramatic dialogue. Omit for ordinary prose.

collapse.description: How many heading levels render as collapsible sections; anything deeper renders as a heading with its content beneath. Omit to collapse at every level, which is the default and right for most texts. 0 renders the whole work as one continuous scroll (Plato's dialogues, Greek tragedy, Epictetus) — use it only where the text is short enough to parse whole, since a flat section is parsed when its parent opens. 1 collapses only the top division and reads continuously inside it (Shakespeare's acts, Pascal's fragments). This is a RENDERING decision only: sections, slugs, contents entries and ?s= deep links exist at every level regardless, so choosing a scroll never costs addressability.

filename.description: Filename of the primary text file in this directory

description.description: One-line description of the work's significance

prerequisites.description: Directory names of immediate predecessor texts (one layer deep, temporally proximal). Chain rather than accumulate — e.g., Maxwell → Einstein special → Einstein general, not Euclid → ... → Einstein.

supplements.description: Directory names of supplements that accompany this text. Populated as supplements are authored.

ocr_status.description: Whether the text is ready to read in clean markdown form. needs-review: produced by the processing pipeline and machine-checked, but not yet read against the source by a person.
